### PHP_CodeSniffer gitblame report command injection via crafted filename
[CVE-2026-67434](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-67434) / [GHSA-hmqg-cxww-wqhq](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hmqg-cxww-wqhq)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

PHP_CodeSniffer versions before v3.13.6 and v4.0.2 contain a command injection vulnerability in the code creating the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` and `Svnblame` report(s).

As a result, running PHP_CodeSniffer over untrusted files, for example, in a CI pipeline that scans pull requests, or on a developer machine reviewing third-party code, could result in attacker-controlled shell commands being executed when the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` or `Svnblame` report(s) would process a file whose name contains shell metacharacters.

* Users using the default `Full` report, or any of the other non-*blame reports, are not affected.
* Users on a runtime platform which does not allow filenames to contain shell metacharacters, such as `"` and `;`, are not affected.

##### Patched versions

The issue has been fixed in PHP_CodeSniffer v3.13.6 and v4.0.2. We recommend all users upgrade to these versions at their earliest convenience.

##### Workaround

Users of PHP_CodeSniffer who cannot upgrade immediately should ensure they do not use the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` or the `Svnblame` reports when scanning untrusted code.

This is especially relevant for CI jobs, pre-commit or review tooling, automated review services, and any service that scans untrusted repositories or uploaded source trees.

##### Credits

Many thanks to both [@​Faze-up](https://redirect.github.com/Faze-up) and [@​edorian](https://redirect.github.com/edorian) for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability.

##### How can I report a security bug?

Please report security vulnerabilities privately via [the "Security and quality" tab on the PHP_CodeSniffer repository](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/security).

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 7.3 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

### [`v3.13.5`](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/releases/tag/3.13.5): - 2025-11-04

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/compare/3.13.4...3.13.5)

##### Added

- Runtime support for PHP 8.5. All known PHP 8.5 deprecation notices have been fixed.
  - Syntax support for new PHP 8.5 features will follow in a future release.
  - If you find any PHP 8.5 deprecation notices which were missed, please report them.

##### Changed

- Various housekeeping, including improvements to the tests and documentation.
  - Thanks to [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) and [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for their contributions.

##### Fixed

- Fixed bug [#​1216](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1216): Tokenizer/PHP: added more defensive coding to prevent PHP 8.5 "Using null as an array offset" deprecation notices.
  - Thanks to [Andrew Lyons](https://redirect.github.com/andrewnicols) for the patch.
- Fixed bug [#​1279](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1279): Tokenizer/PHP: on PHP < 8.0, an unclosed attribute (parse error) could end up removing some tokens from the token stream.
  - This could lead to false positives and false negative from sniffs, but could also lead to incorrect fixes being made mangling the file under scan.
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.

##### Other

- Please be aware that the `master` branch has been renamed to `3.x` and the default branch has changed to the `4.x` branch.
  - If you contribute to PHP\_CodeSniffer, you will need to update your local git clone.
  - If you develop against PHP\_CodeSniffer and run your tests against dev branches of PHPCS, you will need to update your workflows.

### [`v3.13.3`](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/releases/tag/3.13.3): - 2025-09-04

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/compare/3.13.2...3.13.3)

##### Added

- Tokenizer support for PHP 8.4 dereferencing of new expressions without wrapping parentheses. [#​1160](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1160)
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.
- Tokenizer support for PHP 8.4 `abstract` properties. [#​1183](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1183)
  - The `File::getMemberProperties()` method now also supports `abstract` properties through a new `is_abstract` array index in the return value. [#​1184](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1184)
  - Additionally, the following sniffs have been updated to support `abstract` properties:
    - Generic.PHP.LowerCaseConstant [#​1185](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1185)
    - Generic.PHP.UpperCaseConstant [#​1185](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1185)
    - PSR2.Classes.PropertyDeclaration [#​1188](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1188)
    - Squiz.Commenting.VariableComment [#​1186](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1186)
    - Squiz.WhiteSpace.MemberVarSpacing [#​1187](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1187)
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patches
- Tokenizer support for the PHP 8.4 "exit as a function call" change. [#​1201](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1201)
  - When `exit`/`die` is used as a fully qualified "function call", it will now be tokenized as `T_NS_SEPARATOR` + `T_EXIT`.
  - Additionally, the following sniff has been updated to handle fully qualified exit/die correctly:
    - Squiz.PHP.NonExecutableCode
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patches

##### Changed

- Tokenizer/PHP: fully qualified `true`/`false`/`null` will now be tokenized as `T_NS_SEPARATOR` + `T_TRUE`/`T_FALSE`/`T_NULL`. [#​1201](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1201)
  - Previously, these were tokenized as `T_NS_SEPARATOR` + `T_STRING`.
  - Additionally, the following sniffs have been updated to handle fully qualified true/false/null correctly:
    - Generic.CodeAnalysis.UnconditionalIfStatement
    - Generic.ControlStructures.DisallowYodaConditions
    - PEAR.Functions.ValidDefaultValue
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patches.
- Generic.PHP.Syntax: the sniff is now able to scan input provided via STDIN on non-Windows OSes. [#​915](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/915)
  - Thanks to [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) for the patch.
- PSR2.ControlStructures.SwitchDeclaration: the `WrongOpener*` error code is now auto-fixable if the identified "wrong opener" is a semi-colon. [#​1161](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1161)
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.
- The PSR2.Classes.PropertyDeclaration will now check that the abstract modifier keyword is placed before a visibility keyword. [#​1188](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1188)
  - Errors will be reported via a new `AbstractAfterVisibility` error code.
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.
- Various housekeeping, including improvements to the tests and documentation.
  - Thanks to [Bernhard Zwein](https://redirect.github.com/benno5020), [Rick Kerkhof](https://redirect.github.com/NanoSector), [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) and [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for their contributions.

##### Fixed

- Fixed bug [#​1112](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1112) : `--parallel` option fails if PHP\_CodeSniffer is invoked via bash and the invokation creates a non-PHPCS-managed process.
  - Thanks to [Rick Kerkhof](https://redirect.github.com/NanoSector) for the patch.
- Fixed bug [#​1113](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1113) : fatal error when the specified "files to scan" would result in the same file being added multiple times to the queue.
  - This error only occured when `--parallel` scanning was enabled.
  - Thanks to [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) for the patch.
- Fixed bug [#​1154](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1154) : PEAR.WhiteSpace.ObjectOperatorIndent: false positive when checking multiple chained method calls in a multidimensional array.
  - Thanks to [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) for the patch.
- Fixed bug [#​1193](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1193) : edge case inconsistency in how empty string array keys for sniff properties are handled.
  - Thanks to [Rodrigo Primo](https://redirect.github.com/rodrigoprimo) and [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.
- Fixed bug [#​1197](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/1197) : Squiz.Commenting.FunctionComment: return types containing a class name with underscores would be truncated leading to incorrect results.
  - Thanks to [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for the patch.

##### Other

- The [Wiki documentation](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/wiki) is now publicly editable. :tada:
  - Update proposals can be submittted by opening a pull request in the [PHPCSStandards/PHP\_CodeSniffer-documentation](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer-documentation) repository.
    Contributions welcome !
  - Thanks to [Anna Filina](https://redirect.github.com/afilina), [Dan Wallis](https://redirect.github.com/fredden) and [Juliette Reinders Folmer](https://redirect.github.com/jrfnl) for their work on getting this set up.
- The [Phar website](https://phars.phpcodesniffer.com/) has had a facelift. [#​107](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/issues/107)
  - Thanks to [Bernhard Zwein](https://redirect.github.com/benno5020) for making this happen!

### PHP_CodeSniffer gitblame report command injection via crafted filename
[CVE-2026-67434](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-67434) / [GHSA-hmqg-cxww-wqhq](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-hmqg-cxww-wqhq)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Impact

PHP_CodeSniffer versions before v3.13.6 and v4.0.2 contain a command injection vulnerability in the code creating the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` and `Svnblame` report(s).

As a result, running PHP_CodeSniffer over untrusted files, for example, in a CI pipeline that scans pull requests, or on a developer machine reviewing third-party code, could result in attacker-controlled shell commands being executed when the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` or `Svnblame` report(s) would process a file whose name contains shell metacharacters.

* Users using the default `Full` report, or any of the other non-*blame reports, are not affected.
* Users on a runtime platform which does not allow filenames to contain shell metacharacters, such as `"` and `;`, are not affected.

##### Patched versions

The issue has been fixed in PHP_CodeSniffer v3.13.6 and v4.0.2. We recommend all users upgrade to these versions at their earliest convenience.

##### Workaround

Users of PHP_CodeSniffer who cannot upgrade immediately should ensure they do not use the `Gitblame`, `Hgblame` or the `Svnblame` reports when scanning untrusted code.

This is especially relevant for CI jobs, pre-commit or review tooling, automated review services, and any service that scans untrusted repositories or uploaded source trees.

##### Credits

Many thanks to both [@​Faze-up](https://redirect.github.com/Faze-up) and [@​edorian](https://redirect.github.com/edorian) for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability.

##### How can I report a security bug?

Please report security vulnerabilities privately via [the "Security and quality" tab on the PHP_CodeSniffer repository](https://redirect.github.com/PHPCSStandards/PHP_CodeSniffer/security).
